questions.q: What activated the Matternet M2's flight termination system in Zurich?
options: Loss of link with the operator's radio
questions.explain: Vibration grew on all three IMUs, IMU3's data sharply diverged from the other two → EKF divergence → FTS.

questions.q: Why didn't the parachute save the Matternet M2?
options: It was too small for that mass
questions.explain: The line did not withstand the jerk because of prior damage.

questions.q: What did the Airspeeder's controller do on loss of link?
options: Engaged RTH to the takeoff point
questions.explain: It froze the throttle and held level attitude — the aircraft climbed to ~7900 feet. A “hold” failsafe instead of “descend” is the main lesson.

questions.q: Why was the cause of the Airspeeder's loss of link not established?
options: The board did not look for the cause
questions.explain: Without a log, an investigation ends with the words “not established”.

questions.q: What caused the Alta X to crash?
options: Battery depletion because of the threshold
questions.explain: The warning threshold was lowered from 44 to 42 V, the voltage before takeoff was not checked: there was no hardware failure.

questions.q: What impact energy threshold is taken as the risk of serious injury?
questions.explain: The Matternet without cargo is already 118 J.

questions.q: The common conclusion of the three cases:
options: Parachutes are needed on all aircraft
questions.explain: What the aircraft does when something goes wrong is the engineer's main question.

questions.q: Why does an accident analysis look for the root cause in the process rather than in a person?
options: A process can be changed so that the error doesn't repeat with anyone
So that no one is responsible for the accident
questions.explain: Changing the process protects against a repeat regardless of who does the work.
